answer: Port scanning works by determining the status of ports on a remote system. It involves sending requests to various ports to identify which ones are open for communication over TCP or UDP networking. This technique is commonly used in reconnaissance to discover services running on remote hosts and local network devices, which may include vulnerable services that could be exploited. Tools are often employed to perform these scans, which can include vulnerability and wordlist scans as well [Source 1][Source 3].
